name: blackswan-seasonal
description: The CALENDAR / SEASONAL anomaly probe — the famous free date-effects: turn-of-the-month (Ariel 1987; Lakonishok-Smidt 1988), sell-in-May / Halloween (Bouman-Jacobsen 2002), and the Monday effect (French 1980). Each is a deterministic date rule traded as an EXPOSURE-BALANCED calendar SPREAD on SPY: LONG the claimed-good window (scaled +0.5/frequency), SHORT its complement (-0.5/frequency), so the time-averaged net exposure is ZERO and the DSR-deflated oos_sharpe measures the seasonal differential net of cost — isolated from the market's drift (an unequal-window naive spread would be net-directional and merely track the year's beta). signal=seasonal is the published rule; seasonal_inverse is the exact negation (mirror control). The book is a PURE FUNCTION OF THE CALENDAR (never price; mutation-proven), turnover-costed. Deterministic and model-free. DATA: etfs/SPY-1d-*.json.

universe.description: The asset(s) the calendar rule times. spy = the S&P 500 ETF, the equity index where these anomalies are defined. equity_rates / diversified spread the same calendar position equally across a basket.

rule.description: turn_of_month = long the last trading day of the month + first tom_days of the next, short the rest (Lakonishok-Smidt); sell_in_may = long Nov-Apr, short May-Oct (Bouman-Jacobsen); day_of_week = short Monday, long Tue-Fri (French). An unknown rule is refused.

signal.description: seasonal = the published direction (long the good window); seasonal_inverse = the exact negation (mirror control). Pre-registering both prevents post-hoc direction cherry-picking.

tom_days.description: For turn_of_month only: how many trading days at the start of each month are in the window (plus the last trading day of the prior month). 3 is the Lakonishok-Smidt window. Ignored by other rules.

transaction_fee.description: Per-unit-of-turnover cost charged both ways (~0.1% round trip). Seasonal switches are few per year, so cost is small — the null is a gross null.

walk_forward_window.description: Which out-of-sample year is ACCOUNTED. A real calendar edge must clear DSR-Sharpe in a MAJORITY of these 17 years, not one.

seed.description: Present for contract conformance only — the rule is fully deterministic, so seeds are not swept.
